# Architecture catalog

Catalog date: 2026-11-16. For changing B2 product details, use <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning> as the authority.

## Offload drive logs from vehicles and depots into a versioned raw zone

Upload closed rosbag2/MCAP log splits from vehicles, depot ingest stations, or shipped drives into a versioned B2 raw zone, verify each split before deleting the local copy, send only trigger-flagged event windows over the air, and start downstream extraction from object-created events.

**Use when:** Test vehicles continuously record synchronized sensor data in bounded log splits. Offload must never lose a split, keep long-lived credentials off vehicles, keep every version recoverable for audit, notify the pipeline without polling, move years of historic logs, and let engineers preview a drive soon after it lands.

**Workflow:** Record synchronized sensor topics with rosbag2 (MCAP storage) and close a split every N GB or N minutes → Upload only trigger-flagged event windows over cellular; hold full splits for depot Wi-Fi or a drive swap → Request short-lived presigned PUT or multipart part URLs from a fleet API for raw/<date>/<vehicle>/<drive_id>/ → Record the upload version ID; an ingest verifier compares the stored bytes with the source size and SHA-256 before acknowledging local deletion → Sync depot ingest stations and shipped drives with rclone or s5cmd using a write-only key scoped to raw/; seed large backfills with Fireball → Verify signed Event Notifications, check completeness, and mark failed splits as quarantined in the metadata database with a marker object under quarantine/ → Record the drive/session row in the metadata database and export a Parquet copy under catalog/ → Index recordings for triage with a self-hosted Foxglove Edge Site → Server-side copy incident splits to an Object Lock bucket under legal hold

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Presigned PUT (5 GB single-PUT limit) and presigned multipart part uploads, Scoped application keys (write-only ingest key limited to raw/), Event Notifications (prefix-filtered, signed webhook), Server-side copy, Object Lock and legal hold, Lifecycle rules, including cleanup of unfinished multipart uploads, SSE-B2 encryption, Backblaze Fireball bulk ingest.

**Integrations:** [rclone](https://rclone.org/b2/) — Native Backblaze B2 backend (type = b2) with a write-only key scoped to raw/; the S3 backend with the B2 endpoint also works ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-rclone-with-backblaze-b2)); [s5cmd](https://github.com/peak/s5cmd) — Copy closed splits from local disk with --endpoint-url (or S3_ENDPOINT_URL) set to https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com and the depot's write-only key; size --numworkers, cp --concurrency, and --part-size to the depot uplink ([setup guide](https://github.com/peak/s5cmd#readme)); [Foxglove Edge Site (self-hosted)](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/data/edge-sites/installation) — recordingStorage.provider=s3_compatible with recordingStorage.s3CompatibleServiceUrl set to the B2 S3 endpoint and an HMAC key pair in the recording-storage-credentials secret; set recordingStorage.s3CompatibleServiceRegion to the bucket region.

**Scale:** Fleet recording rates, logging hours, and retention determine the raw corpus size. Depot uplink bandwidth and upload concurrency usually bound ingest; measure before considering Overdrive, and use Fireball for historic backfills.

**Security:** Vehicles never hold application keys; they receive presigned URLs scoped to one object key with short expiry; The fleet API key has writeFiles only on raw/; upload responses, not HeadObject, confirm completion; writeFiles keys can hide or supersede raw files; versions stay recoverable, and default governance retention on the raw bucket adds immutability where the program requires it; Depot keys are write-only (writeFiles, listFiles at most) and scoped to raw/; Verify the X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature HMAC and make consumers idempotent; Keep Object Lock and legal-hold credentials out of ingest services.

## Decode drive logs into a queryable sensor lake and mine long-tail scenarios

Extract raw logs into per-topic Parquet/Iceberg tables and frame blobs on B2, query them in place with Spark, Trino, or DuckDB, find rare scenarios with embedding search over keyframes, and freeze results as versioned scenario-set manifests.

**Use when:** Raw logs are not searchable. Engineers need SQL over billions of frame and event rows and semantic search over camera clips without copying petabytes of blobs into a warehouse or running a permanent cluster.

**Workflow:** Read raw splits with range GETs using the MCAP chunk index; decode and time-synchronize topics → Write extracted/<topic>/ Parquet and frame blobs with lineage back to the source split → Register Apache Iceberg tables under warehouse/ in a separate SQL or REST catalog → Run rule-based scene detectors in Spark or Trino; use DuckDB for ad hoc analyst queries → Embed keyframes and store a LanceDB table and ANN index under embeddings/ → Write query results as immutable scenarios/<set>/<version>/manifest.json → Serve previews with short-lived presigned GET URLs

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Range GETs (MCAP chunk-indexed reads), Presigned GET URLs for previews, Scoped application keys per zone (read-only raw/, read-write extracted/ and warehouse/), Object versioning and lifecycle rules, SSE-B2 encryption.

**Integrations:** [Apache Spark (Hadoop S3A)](https://hadoop.apache.org/docs/stable/hadoop-aws/tools/hadoop-aws/index.html) — fs.s3a.endpoint=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com with fs.s3a.endpoint.region and fs.s3a.path.style.access=true, plus per-bucket endpoint and credential overrides for the raw and lake buckets ([setup guide](https://hadoop.apache.org/docs/current/hadoop-aws/tools/hadoop-aws/third_party_stores.html)); [Trino](https://trino.io/) — Native S3 file system (fs.s3.enabled=true) with s3.endpoint set to B2, s3.region set to the bucket region, and s3.path-style-access=true in each Iceberg, Hive, or Delta Lake catalog ([setup guide](https://trino.io/docs/current/object-storage/file-system-s3.html)); [DuckDB (httpfs)](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/httpfs/s3api.html) — S3 secret with ENDPOINT set to the B2 host name (s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com, no scheme), REGION, URL_STYLE 'path', and a read-only lake key; [Apache Iceberg (PyIceberg)](https://py.iceberg.apache.org/configuration/) — FileIO s3.endpoint set to the B2 endpoint and s3.region to the bucket region; run the SQL or REST catalog separately; [LanceDB / Lance](https://lancedb.com/) — Use the pinned LanceDB 0.20.0 / pylance 0.23.2 connection profile in examples/lancedb.md, with the B2 endpoint, region and scoped credentials; serialize all table mutations through one writer service ([setup guide](https://github.com/lance-format/lance/blob/v0.23.2/rust/lance-table/src/io/commit.rs)).

**Scale:** Billions of frame and event rows; millions of keyframe embeddings; petabytes of referenced blobs. Query engines read Parquet footers and row groups with range GETs. Size Parquet files and row groups to avoid many tiny requests; consider Overdrive only when sustained scan throughput, not compute, is the bottleneck.

**Security:** Extraction jobs hold three keys (read-only raw/, extract-writer on extracted/, and iceberg-writer on warehouse/) because a key has one name prefix; Analyst DuckDB sessions use a read-only key scoped to the lake bucket, never raw/; Treat preview URLs as bearer credentials with short expiry.

## Anonymize, pre-label, and annotate camera and LiDAR frames, then publish versioned label sets

Blur faces and license plates in selected camera frames, run model-assisted 2D and 3D pre-labeling, have humans refine labels in tools that read media from B2 directly or through presigned URLs, and write versioned label releases back to B2.

**Use when:** Labeling campaigns cover tens of thousands to millions of synchronized LiDAR sweeps and multi-camera frames. Copying them into each vendor's storage adds cost, delay, and privacy risk, and label exports need versioning tied to the scenario set they came from.

**Workflow:** Select frames, LiDAR sweeps, calibration, and ego-pose from a frozen scenario manifest → Write face- and plate-blurred copies to anonymized/<campaign>/ → Write pre-labels from 3D detectors, SAM 2, and trackers to prelabels/<campaign>/ → Attach the bucket to CVAT or Label Studio as S3-compatible storage, or register presigned URLs with Segments.ai or Encord → Run QA and dataset slicing in FiftyOne Enterprise against the same bucket → Export annotations to labels/<campaign>/<version>/ and write the checksummed manifest last → Start validation and dataset assembly from the manifest's Event Notification

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Presigned GET URLs and bucket CORS rules for browser labeling tools, Scoped application keys (read-only anonymized/ for labeling tools, write-only labels/), Event Notifications, Object versioning, SSE-B2 encryption.

**Integrations:** [CVAT](https://docs.cvat.ai/docs/workspace/attach-cloud-storage/) — Attach cloud storage with the Amazon S3 provider, the required Endpoint URL set to the B2 endpoint, and a read-only key scoped to anonymized/ ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-connect-backblaze-b2-cloud-storage-to-cvat)); [Label Studio](https://labelstud.io/guide/storage_s3) — Amazon S3 source and target storage with the S3 Endpoint field set to the B2 endpoint; a read-only key on anonymized/ for source and a separate writer on labels/ for target; [Segments.ai](https://docs.segments.ai/how-to-integrate/import-data) — Customer-secured URLs; your service signs B2 GET URLs with a read-only anonymized/ key and registers them on samples, refreshing open samples before the 7-day SigV4 maximum; [Encord](https://docs.encord.com/platform-documentation/General/annotate-data-integrations/annotate-direct-access-integration) — Direct Access integration; register files with a JSON whose objectUrl values are presigned B2 GET URLs signed by your service, add bucket CORS for the Encord origin, and re-sign before the 7-day SigV4 maximum. Encord's S3-compatible (MinIO) integration is the alternative when Encord may hold a read-only key and sign URLs itself; [FiftyOne Enterprise](https://docs.voxel51.com/enterprise/installation.html) — MinIO credentials profile (MINIO_ENDPOINT_URL or an ini endpoint_url) set to the B2 endpoint, plus region and a read-only key; media paths use the endpoint as their prefix.

**Scale:** Tens of thousands to millions of synchronized LiDAR sweeps and multi-camera frames per campaign. Annotator latency depends on the labeling tool and browser path, not Overdrive. Pre-label and anonymization jobs are throughput-bound GPU batch work.

**Security:** Labeling tool keys read only anonymized/ and prelabels/, never raw/; Label export keys write only to labels/<campaign>/; CORS allows exact tool origins, not *; Presigned URLs given to external vendors are bearer credentials; keep expiry to the labeling window.

## Version perception datasets, stream them to training, and track checkpoints

Freeze labeled scenarios into immutable dataset versions (manifests plus shards) on B2, pin them with lakeFS or DVC, stream shards directly into training, and persist Ray Train checkpoints and MLflow run artifacts to B2.

**Use when:** Perception datasets range from tens of terabytes to petabytes and change constantly. Teams need reproducible versions that tie each model to its drives, labels, and splits, streaming without full local copies, and durable checkpoints for multi-node runs.

**Workflow:** Assemble nuScenes/KITTI-style manifests and WebDataset or Parquet shards into datasets/<name>/<version>/, manifest last → Commit the version on a lakeFS branch over the B2 blockstore, or pin manifests in git with a DVC S3 remote → Stream shards to Ray Train or PyTorch workers with per-worker S3 GETs and local NVMe only as cache → Persist Ray Train checkpoints to s3://<bucket>/checkpoints/<run> with endpoint_override → Log metrics, evaluation reports, and registered models to an MLflow b2:// artifact store → Server-side copy released datasets and models to an Object Lock bucket; expire intermediate checkpoints by lifecycle sized above the longest run plus resume window

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, High-concurrency streaming GETs, Multipart upload for large checkpoints, Scoped application keys (read-only datasets/ for training, write-only checkpoints/), Server-side copy, Object Lock for released datasets and models, Lifecycle rules for intermediate checkpoints, Presigned URLs for dataset delivery to partners.

**Integrations:** [Ray (Train)](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/user-guides/persistent-storage.html) — Set RunConfig storage_path to an s3:// URI with endpoint_override=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com, or set AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 with a plain s3:// path; [MLflow](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/) — Native b2://<bucket>@<endpoint-host>/<path> artifact store, or an s3:// artifact root with MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL set to the B2 endpoint; use proxied artifact access so only the tracking server holds the key ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-connect-backblaze-b2-to-mlflow)); [lakeFS](https://docs.lakefs.io/reference/configuration/) — Blockstore type s3 with blockstore.s3.endpoint set to the B2 endpoint, blockstore.s3.force_path_style=true, and the bucket region ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lakefs-integration-with-backblaze-b2)); [DVC](https://doc.dvc.org/user-guide/data-management/remote-storage/amazon-s3) — S3 remote (dvc remote add) with endpointurl set to the B2 endpoint and credentials stored with --local.

**Scale:** Tens of terabytes to petabytes per dataset; multi-node GPU training reading shards in parallel. Shard size and per-worker concurrency determine throughput. Measure GPU utilization with Standard B2 first; evaluate Overdrive when sustained read throughput is the proven bottleneck.

**Security:** Training jobs read datasets/ with a read-only key and write only to checkpoints/; Release publication and Object Lock credentials stay outside training clusters; the publisher key covers the source and release buckets for server-side copy; Partner dataset delivery uses presigned URLs from a read-only key scoped to one dataset version.

## Re-simulate real drives and synthetic scenarios against each stack build and keep comparable KPIs

Store scenario definitions and a frozen regression suite on B2, replay real log splits to re-sim workers from presigned URLs, write simulator episodes back to B2, and keep per-build KPI results immutable and comparable across releases.

**Use when:** Every stack release must be checked against thousands of real and synthetic scenarios. Re-sim needs fast read access to raw splits without copying them or giving workers broad keys, simulator output is terabyte-scale per run, and results must be reproducible and auditable per build.

**Workflow:** Version scenario configs (OpenSCENARIO or CARLA/ScenarioRunner) and a regression-suite manifest on B2 → Trigger a run from CI and fan scenarios out to re-sim and simulator workers with an orchestrator such as Ray Core (no B2 connection of its own) → Give re-sim workers presigned GET URLs for raw splits; pull or range-read to local NVMe and replay with ros2 bag play → Write synthetic episodes to sim/episodes/<build>/<scenario>/<id>/ → Write per-run KPIs as Parquet under sim/results/<build>/ and log them to MLflow per build → Copy release-candidate results to an Object Lock bucket as safety-case evidence; expire bulk synthetic frames → Promote curated synthetic episodes into training datasets

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Presigned GET URLs (maximum 7-day expiry) for replay manifests, Range GETs, Scoped application keys (read-only raw/ held by the orchestrator to sign URLs, write-only sim/ for workers), Object Lock for release-candidate evaluation results, Lifecycle rules for bulk synthetic frames.

**Integrations:** [MLflow](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/) — Native b2://<bucket>@<endpoint-host>/<path> artifact store, or an s3:// artifact root with MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL set to the B2 endpoint; use proxied artifact access so only the tracking server holds the key ([setup guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-connect-backblaze-b2-to-mlflow)).

**Scale:** Thousands of scenarios per build; terabytes of simulator output per run. Re-sim reads whole splits once per scenario; synthetic writes are bursty. Expire bulk synthetic frames and keep KPI tables small and permanent.

**Security:** Re-sim workers receive presigned GET URLs, not raw/ read keys; Simulator and re-sim workers write only to sim/ with a write-only key; Only the release pipeline can copy into the Object Lock evidence bucket, with one publisher key covering the sim and evidence buckets.

## Related sample applications

Sample applications for these storage workflows. Each linked repository includes source code and setup instructions.

- [Rosbag2 Cloud Offload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/rosbag2-cloud-offload): Presigned-PUT offload of closed rosbag2 splits with head_object verification before local delete, a Parquet session catalog, and a presigned-GET replay manifest.
- [Roboflow Inference Frame Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/roboflow-inference-frame-archive): Edge inference that archives only flagged frames and predictions to B2 with Parquet roll-ups.
- [CLIP Video Scene Search](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/clip-video-scene-search): PySceneDetect segmentation and OpenCLIP text/image scene search over a FAISS index stored on B2.
- [YOLO Drone and Dashcam Footage Detection](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/yolo-drone-footage-detection): Multipart upload of dashcam or drone video, YOLO detection on keyframes, and GPS-correlated GeoJSON detections on B2.
- [SAM 2 Mask Dataset Builder](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/sam2-mask-dataset-builder): SAM 2 mask propagation across video, written to B2 as versioned COCO RLE segmentation datasets.
- [ByteTrack Dataset Builder](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/bytetrack-dataset-builder): Versioned MOT tracking datasets built from raw video on B2.
- [YOLO11 Batch Detection Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/yolo11-batch-detection-pipeline): Batch 2D detection and segmentation over B2 image and video libraries producing COCO JSON pre-labels and crops.
- [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker): Verifies and fans out signed B2 Event Notifications to subscribers.
- [b2listen](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2listen): Forwards B2 Event Notifications to local services during development (not listed in the Labs feed).
- [DuckDB Query In Place](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/duckdb-query-in-place): SQL over Parquet, CSV, and JSON in B2 through DuckDB httpfs with a custom endpoint.
- [Iceberg Feature Store](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/iceberg-feature-store): PyIceberg tables on B2 with a local SQL catalog, schema evolution, snapshot rollback, and DuckDB time travel.
- [Lance Multimodal Search](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lance-multimodal-search): A LanceDB vector table and ANN index stored directly on B2 next to the media.
- [WebDataset Streaming PyTorch Training](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/webdataset-streaming-pytorch-training): Tar shards streamed from B2 into PyTorch with worker and node shard splits and no local staging.
- [lakeFS on B2 Quickstart](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lakefs-on-b2-quickstart): lakeFS branch, commit, and merge over a B2 blockstore (public repo, not listed in the Labs feed).
- [fastdup Dataset Cleaning](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/fastdup-dataset-cleaning): Duplicate, outlier, and broken-frame detection on B2 with quarantine instead of deletion.
- [nuScenes Sensor Data Lake](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/nuscenes-sensor-data-lake): nuScenes-format camera, LiDAR, and radar blobs on B2 indexed with the devkit and served as presigned per-keyframe training manifests.
- [MMDetection3D LiDAR Dataset](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/mmdetection3d-lidar-dataset): KITTI-style LiDAR turned into 3D detection datasets with pre-labels, manifests, and checkpoints on B2.
- [KISS-ICP LiDAR Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/kiss-icp-lidar-archive): KISS-ICP LiDAR odometry and incremental mapping with raw scans, poses, .ply map snapshots, and trajectories archived per session on B2.
- [CARLA Sensor Data Lake](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/carla-sensor-data-lake): CARLA scenario configs and per-episode sensor frames on B2 served to a PyTorch DataLoader with presigned URLs.
